data.narrative:
Cerebras is a publicly traded semiconductor company founded by Andrew Feldman and four co-founders. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage, same-sector public comparables in Chips & Semiconductors: Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B).

The peer-median method is applicable and yields an implied valuation of $2.3B. This median anchors the analysis given the broad range observed across the three peers ($1.1B to $35.8B), reflecting material heterogeneity in the sector. A public-comp anchoring approach using price-to-sales multiples from NVDA, AMD, and ALAB (median P/S of 20.4x) cannot be applied; Cerebras' revenue is not disclosed and private companies rarely make such figures available. With only one triangulation method yielding a reliable result, the analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B to $2.6B (median $2.3B).

The current public valuation of $39.2B sits substantially above this peer-median estimate. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the three chosen public comparables to Cerebras' specific technology and market position, the limited methodological breadth available without disclosed financials, and potential selection bias in the peer set. Revenue disclosure or forward guidance would enable revenue-multiple cross-validation and narrow the range materially.
